alerts.title: Weight gain attribution unclear
alerts.message: Guidelines note an association between DTG and abnormal weight gain, but state the association may not be causal and could be due to less metabolic toxicity compared to older regimens. The patient has gained 12 kg since starting TLD (DTG-based regimen) 3 years ago, with a current BMI of 33. However, the patient also has poorly controlled hypothyroidism (TSH 12.4 mIU/L), which is a known non-drug cause of weight gain, tiredness, and constipation.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimize levothyroxine therapy for hypothyroidism before attributing weight gain solely to DTG.

alerts.title: Hyperglycemia screening indicated
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking glucose for patients transitioning to DTG if they have two or more risk factors for hyperglycemia. This patient has two risk factors: age ≥30 years and BMI ≥25 kg/m² (BMI is 33). Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, which is within the normal range, but ongoing monitoring is advised due to persistent risk factors.

evidence.recommended_action: Follow guideline flowchart: check glucose due to presence of ≥2 risk factors for hyperglycemia.

alerts.title: Hypothyroidism uncontrolled
alerts.message: The patient's hypothyroidism is poorly controlled with TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5) and low Free T4, with reported non-adherence to levothyroxine. Symptoms of tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, and periorbital puffiness are consistent with this. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism contributes to weight gain and dyslipidemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Reinforce levothyroxine adherence, consider dose adjustment, and recheck TSH in 6-8 weeks.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking viral load every 6 months for patients on DTG-based ART, or every 12 months if VL <50 copies/mL for >1 year with reliable adherence. The last viral load was 106 days ago (over 3 months) and was <50 copies/mL. The patient's adherence is uncertain ('often forgets the thyroid tablet'). A plan for the next VL test is not stated.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load test per guideline frequency (6 or 12 monthly based on adherence history).
